You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository fastapi/fastapi.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix using class (not instance) dependency that has `__call__` method

As reported in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14452, FastAPI 0.123.6 introduced a regression - if we use class (not instance) as dependency and this class has `__call__` method that is coroutine or generator, it is mistakenly treated as coroutine\generator (actually class is not coroutine\generator, instance of this class is).


So, to fix this we need to check if the callable is class before inspecting its `dunder_call` in `is_coroutine_callable`, `is_async_gen_callable`, and `is_gen_callable`.

Okay, I see the logic. In `is_gen_callable`, `is_async_gen_callable`, and `is_coroutine_callable`, it checks `self.call` and then it checks `getattr(..., "__call__", None)`.

If `self.call` is a class, then `self.call.__call__` is the method that will be called when an instance of the class is called. But the issue says that if we use a class as a dependency, it should not be treated as a coroutine/generator just because its `__call__` method is one. The class itself is not a coroutine/generator; only its instances (when called) might be.

Wait, if `self.call` is a class, then `self.call` is callable. When FastAPI calls it, it will create an instance of the class. If the class has a `__call__` method, that's for the *instance*.

The issue says: "if we use class (not instance) as dependency and this class has `__call__` method that is coroutine or generator, it is mistakenly treated as coroutine\generator (actually class is not coroutine\generator, instance of this class is)."

So if `inspect.isclass(self.call)` is true, we should skip the `__call__` check.

steps.message:
Wait, `Class is_coroutine_callable: True`. This is exactly the bug. If `MyClass` is used as a dependency, FastAPI will think it's a coroutine function and will `await` it. But `MyClass()` (the result of calling the class) is an instance of `MyClass`. If `MyClass` has a `__call__` method, that's for the instance.

Wait, if `self.call` is `MyClass`, then `self.call()` returns an instance of `MyClass`.
If `MyClass` has a `__call__` method, then `MyClass()()` would call that method.

FastAPI dependencies are called as `await dep(request, ...)` if they are async, or `dep(request, ...)` if they are sync.

If `dep` is `MyClass`, then `dep(request, ...)` returns an instance of `MyClass`. It does NOT call `MyClass.__call__`.

So `is_coroutine_callable` should be `False` for a class, even if it has a `__call__` method that is a coroutine.

Let's check `is_gen_callable` and `is_async_gen_callable` too.

The diff looks correct. I have added `if inspect.isclass(self.call): return False` in all three methods before the `__call__` checks.

I'll submit the patch.

I have successfully fixed the regression where classes used as dependencies were mistakenly treated as coroutines or generators if they had a `__call__` method. I added a check to ensure that if the dependency is a class, it is not treated as such, as only instances of the class would be called via `__call__`.

The bug was caused by `is_coroutine_callable`, `is_async_gen_callable`, and `is_gen_callable` in `fastapi/dependencies/models.py` incorrectly inspecting the `__call__` method of a class when that class was used as a dependency. Since FastAPI instantiates the class when it's used as a dependency, the class itself is not a coroutine or generator, even if its `__call__` method is. I added a check `if inspect.isclass(self.call): return False` before the `__call__` inspection in all three methods to fix this regression.
